issues.display_title: Issue #1299: API Get Panorama Manual Blur
issues.main_description_html:
Description

Alongside the backend fixes for the blur processing, several UI updates are required on the Blur section interface (Anonymize 360 Images) to improve usability and remove non-functional features.

Sub-tasks

  • Backend API ready: GET /panoramas/manual-blur/{mid} returns { panos: [{ pano_id, blur_count }] } (panos without blur omitted) for the indicator.

Demo from Developer

Backend endpoint for the manual-blur indicator is implemented and merged to main.

  • Endpoint: GET /panoramas/manual-blur/{mid}
  • Auth: auth middleware (raw token in Authorization header, no Bearer prefix) + moderation-ownership check.
  • Behavior: Reads the 8_blooring table and returns, per panorama, the number of manual-blur regions. Panoramas without blur are omitted.
  • Response (decrypted): 
    {
  "messages": "Data retrieved successfully.",
  "panos": [
    { "pano_id": 12, "blur_count": 3 },
    { "pano_id": 18, "blur_count": 1 }
  ]
}
  • Errors: 409 TOURS.MODERATION_NOT_OWNER (not owner / not found), 401 (missing/invalid token).
  • Architecture: Strict ADR (Controller -> Action -> DTO -> Repository) in the Panoramas domain; encrypted response envelope.
  • Docs: docs/v2/panoramas/get-manual-blur.md, ADR_MIGRATED_APIS.md (#30).

      "messages": "Failed to send update notification",
      "reason": "notify_failed"
    }

Result: Fail. Documented real-data payload does not complete successfully.

Source/Contract Evidence

  • Route exists: POST /photographers/profile/notify-update -> Photographers\Profiles\NotifyUpdateController@handle.
  • Controller builds NotifyUpdateDto, passes auth user_id, and wraps success with ResponseEnvelopeHelper::responseMessages.
  • Action calls NotifyUpdateDto::toPayload(), then ProfileService::notifyUpdate().
  • Service calls upstream POST {BASE_URL_PHOTOGRAPHER}/v1/photographers/{userId}/notify-update.
  • Docs and collection document request body as { "changedFields": { ... } }.
  • Unit tests expect upstream payload ['changedFields' => ['fullname' => 'Ada']].

Bug Notes

  • Fail: NotifyUpdateDto::fromArray() currently uses array_diff_key($data, ['user_id' => null]), so a documented request body { "changedFields": { ... } } becomes changedFields.changedFields after toPayload() instead of forwarding the inner changed fields directly.
  • Fail: Empty request body {} is not treated as empty. After user_id injection, the DTO keeps no real changed field but still creates a payload, causing a 502 notify_failed instead of the documented 400 empty_payload.
  • Fail: Live real-data documented payload returns 502 notify_failed, confirming the endpoint is not usable as documented.

Recommended Fix

  • Update NotifyUpdateDto::fromArray() to read $data['changedFields'] ?? [] directly.
  • Filter null values inside that object only.
  • Keep returning [] when changedFields is missing, empty, or all-null so EmptyPayloadException maps to 400.
  • Add/update unit test for documented body { changedFields: { email: ... } } and empty {}.

Conclusion:

  • Issue #1291 is not fully implemented. Route, ADR structure, docs, and upstream service wiring exist, but the request body is transformed incorrectly and live real-data API requests fail for both empty and documented payload cases.

  • Update Payload for blur_requests: Additionally, fix the messaging to the blur_requests queue. The expected payload must look like this: 
    {
  "pano_id": "47434272",
  "types": ["face"]
}

  1. Authenticated face blur request with real data

Request:

{
  "endpoint": "POST /tours/ai-blur",

    "panos": [47434272],
    "moderation_id": 3540876,

  "pano_id": "47434272",
  "types": ["face"]
}

Response:

  "status": 409,
  "body": {
    "statusCode": 409,
    "data": {
      "messages": "This Constellation does not belong to you, please do not try to hack us!",
      "input": []
    }
  }
}

Result: Pass for controlled API behavior; request is blocked by ownership with the current test account before queuing.

Source/Contract Evidence

  • Route exists: POST /tours/ai-blur -> Tours\Blur\BlurController@aiBlur.
  • API validates type as only plate, face, or both.
  • API creates a job for ai_blur.
  • Worker consumes ai_blur and publishes one payload per panorama to blur_requests.
  • Worker payload shape has the required top-level keys: 
    {
  "pano_id": "<pano id>",
  "types": [...]
}

Bug Notes

  • Fail: app/Workers/Blur/ai_blur.php::processPanoAndSendToQueue() still maps type=plate to: 
    {
  "types": ["license"]
}
  • Fail: type=both still maps to: 
    {
  "types": ["face", "license"]
}
  • Issue #1298 asks for the blur_requests payload to use types, and the public API already accepts type=plate, not type=license. The downstream queue payload should therefore use "plate" consistently.
  • This likely explains the developer note: the JSON shape is present, but blur can still fail if the worker receiving blur_requests expects "plate" while this worker sends "license".

Recommended Fix

  • In app/Workers/Blur/ai_blur.php::processPanoAndSendToQueue():
    • Change case "plate" from ["license"] to ["plate"].
    • Change case "both" from ["face", "license"] to ["face", "plate"].
  • Add a unit/source-level test for blur_requests payload mapping for face, plate, and both.

Conclusion:

  • Issue #1298 is not fully implemented. The queue payload has the requested pano_id and types keys, and face is correct, but plate and both still send the old "license" type to blur_requests.

Description

Backend changes have been implemented to allow Google Stats and TourMkr stats to be accessible via custom whitelabel domains. Each whitelabel account has it's own domain.

the rule is:

  • https://gstats.co/stats_b3c5a32690225492598b809b4df92b92 -> https://www.virtuo-reality.com/stats-b3c5a32690225492598b809b4df92b92

GET /portfolios/gstats?cid=128158523644165989

We now need to update the frontend UI so that the buttons directing users to these stats use their configured whitelabel domain instead of the default application domain. This UI change must be conditionally applied based on the user's subscription tier and domain settings.

Business Logic & Conditions

The link replacement logic should ONLY trigger if the user meets both of the following criteria:

  1. Subscription Tier: The account is currently on the Agency OR Yearly Agency plan.
  2. Configuration: The account has a valid whitelabel domain set up.

Acceptance Criteria

  1. For Agency/Yearly Agency accounts WITH a whitelabel domain: Clicking "Tour Stats" or "Google Stats" successfully redirects the user to the stats page hosted on their specific whitelabel domain.
  2. For all other accounts (or Agency accounts without a whitelabel domain setup): Clicking those same buttons redirects the user to the standard, default stats URL.
  3. The UI rendering and link replacement do not cause noticeable delays or layout shifts on the My Tours or Virtual Tour Manager pages.

    https://{whitelabel}/stats_{session_id}

    • agency without whitelabel -> default https://gstats.co/stats_{session_id},
    • non-agency -> default https://gstats.co/stats_{session_id},
    • missing/unknown CID -> controlled error.
